message.content: /unattended:interview I have a messy CSV at ./data/contacts.csv, a monthly export of about 400 rows: names in mixed case, stray spaces, phone numbers in different formats. I want a tidy copy. The phone cleanup goes through the PhoneFix API, one call per row, which bills $0.02 per call on my account; I accept that, it is the whole point. I keep runs in ./run/ and this run's folder is ./run/2026-11-12-contacts-tidy/. I only want the brief, do not start the work.

content.text:
Before I search or draft anything, three questions, each with my proposed answer:

1. What the tidy copy is for. Proposal: so you can import it into your address book without duplicates or bad numbers.
2. What tidy means for names. Proposal: trim stray spaces, collapse double spaces, and title-case each name.
3. What tidy means for phone numbers. Proposal: every number written as ###-###-####, assuming all are US numbers.

message.content: 1 yes. 2 yes, but leave names that are ALL CAPS and one word alone, those are company names. 3 yes, and a number that cannot be read as ten digits stays as it is and goes on a list.

content.text:
Thanks, those are settled and written down in the rulings file. Next batch, two things, each with my proposed answer:

1. How we will know it works. Proposal: on the 400 rows, every name and number matches the rules above, the row count is unchanged, and the unreadable numbers are listed one per line in ./out/unreadable.txt.
2. What must not change. Proposal: ./data/contacts.csv is never edited; the tidy copy goes to ./out/contacts_tidy.csv, and no email address is touched.

message.content: 1 yes. 2 yes, and keep the column order exactly as it is.

content.text:
Settled and recorded. Last batch, three things, each with my proposed answer:

1. If it fails. Proposal: if the tidy copy still breaks a rule after three honest attempts, stop and report the row numbers that break it; do not loosen a rule to make it pass.
2. What the run may touch. Proposal: it may create and edit files only in ./out and its own run folder, and may run python; it may not delete or overwrite anything in ./data.
3. What the run may reach. Proposal: only what you have already named above; no posts, no messages, no pushes.
